**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

I checked every place a Customer-payable stipulated amount could hide:

- **Fee/payment mechanics (Art. V, p0050–p0070 and the volume tiers):** purely usage-based per-US$1m trade fees, a $35,000 initial payment, and $2,500/month support (p0086). No minimum volume commitment and no shortfall charge. The one "in no event … less than" floor (p0070) is drafted against the *Licensor* and in substance is only a true-up to actual recorded trade volume — not a liquidated sum.
- **"Supplemental Payments" (p0074, p0078):** a 33% revenue share on amounts we actually *receive* from third parties, payable only within 10 days of receipt — contingent on collection, not a penalty.
- **Termination (Art. IV p0049, Art. XX–XXI p0134–p0138):** no early-termination fee, no acceleration of remaining term fees; Licensor only retains the right to be paid for trades already performed. Art. XXIII (p0142) affirmatively bars termination damages against either party.
- **Remedies/indemnity (Art. XI–XIII):** injunctive relief and indemnity, but no pre-agreed damages figure.
- **Audit costs (p0064):** shifting audit cost to us on a >5% discrepancy is an audit-cost allocation, not a liquidated damages or penalty payment, so it sits outside this rule (worth watching under an audit-rights rule if that threshold matters to you).

The rebate/bonus share arrangements (p0075–p0076) run in our favour, so nothing to flag there. Since the preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Licensee — is already satisfied, I made no edit.
